findings.body:
This is not a pure restructure: `fetchUser` now passes `{ timeout: 250 }` to `http.get`. A 250ms budget is very tight for a `/users/:id` round-trip — under normal latency, TLS, or a cold backend the request will abort and surface as a timeout error even when the API is healthy.

Either drop the options object to keep the move behavior-preserving, or pick a production-realistic timeout (and document why) if the deadline is intentional.

summary:
## Verdict

Sneaky behavior change under a rename-only framing — the 250ms timeout on `fetchUser` needs a second look before merge.

## Notes

The PR moves `src/a.ts` → `src/lib/a.ts` and is described as "Restructure only," but the single-line body also passes `{ timeout: 250 }` into `http.get`. That is a runtime contract change, not a pure move.

No other files exist in this tree, so import-path fallout from the rename is not observable here. `http` is still referenced with no import or definition in the file (pre-existing on the base side); worth fixing when this module is wired up for real.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: `src/lib/a.ts` defines `fetchUser` as `http.get(`/users/${id}`, { timeout: 250 })`. The 250ms client timeout is present in the head code; nothing in the tree contradicts that this budget is unusually tight for a normal `/users/:id` round-trip.
